title: English to Marathi: Greetings & Introducing Yourself
description: Say hello, give your name and ask how someone is -- six real Marathi sentences with English meanings, speaking tips and pronunciation support.
intro: Six complete Marathi sentences from Unit 01 for your first conversations: greeting someone, giving your name, asking how they are, and saying what you need. Each row shows the Marathi, its English meaning, and a speaking tip.

One structural heads-up before the table: Marathi puts the verb at the end. "My name is Rahul" becomes माझं नाव राहुल आहे -- the आहे (is) closes the sentence. Every row below follows that pattern, so after six sentences the order starts feeling normal.
tip: नमस्कार works at any hour -- mornings add शुभ सकाळ, nights add शुभ रात्री.

sections.heading: The verb goes last
paragraphs: English says "I am eating"; Marathi says मी खातो आहे -- literally "I eating am". Read each sentence in the table to its final word; the verb is always waiting there.
The need-pattern is softer than English "I want": मला पाणी पाहिजे is more like "to me, water is needed". Use it freely -- it is polite by default.

mistakes.wrong: Keeping English word order: "मी आहे तयार"
mistakes.why: Marathi is subject–object–verb; the verb closes every sentence.

mistakes.wrong: Using नमस्ते because you know Hindi
mistakes.why: Understood, but नमस्कार is the Marathi greeting -- singles you out as a learner otherwise.

mcq.question: "My name is Rahul" in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: Name, then आहे closes the sentence.

translate.note: Unit 01 -- the dative need-pattern: "to me, water is needed".

faq.question: How do you introduce yourself in Marathi?
faq.answer: नमस्कार! माझं नाव ... आहे. (Hello! My name is ...) -- both patterns are in the table above, from Unit 01 of the course.

faq.question: Is Marathi hard for English speakers?
faq.answer: The script and verb-final order are new, but greetings and first sentences are six patterns you can memorize today -- the table above is exactly that set.

title: English to Marathi: Question Words (काय, कुठे, कधी)
description: Ask what, where, when, how, who and why in Marathi -- काय, कुठे, कधी, कसे, कोण, का -- with real questions and answers from the curriculum.
secondaryKeywords: how to ask questions in marathi
intro: Six Marathi question words -- काय (what), कुठे (where), कधी (when), कसे (how), कोण (who), का (why) -- each shown inside a real question-and-answer pair from Unit 07 of the Bol Marathi course.

The grammar is friendlier than English here: no do-support, no inversion. The question word simply sits where the answer will go, and the verb stays at the end: कुठे जात आहेस? पुणे. (Where are you going? Pune.)
tip: Attach each question word to one verb you know: कुठे जात आहेस? कधी येत आहेस? -- six words become six usable questions.

sections.heading: No inversion, no do-support
paragraphs: English rebuilds the sentence to ask a question ("You are going" → "Where are you going?"). Marathi doesn't: statement and question share the same skeleton, and intonation plus the question word do the work.
All six words begin with क -- a family resemblance that makes them fast to memorize as a set.

mistakes.wrong: Moving the verb forward like English
mistakes.right: तू कुठे जात आहेस?, never “कुठे आहेस जात”
mistakes.why: The verb-final rule never bends, even in questions.
English “What is it like?” tempts काय everywhere -- but asking about manner is कसे: कसे आहे? (How is it?)

mcq.question: How do you ask “when” in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: कधी (kadhī) = when -- कधी येत आहेस? उद्या.

mcq.question: कोण हे तो? asks…
mcq.explanation: कोण = who. Answer in the lesson: माझा मित्र (my friend).

fill.hint: The answer is a time, so ask about time.

faq.question: What is “what” in Marathi?
faq.answer: काय (kāy). “What is this?” is काय है? -- the first question in Unit 07.

faq.question: Do Marathi questions change word order?
faq.answer: Never. The question word replaces the answer in place and the verb stays final: कधी येत आहेस? उद्या.

title: English to Marathi: Introducing Yourself & Meeting People
description: How to say your name, where you are from, what you do, and ask about others -- real Unit 01 & 05 sentences with English meanings.
secondaryKeywords: where are you from in marathi
intro: Eight Marathi sentences for introducing yourself and learning about others: giving your name, stating your city, saying what you do, asking names and origins. All from Units 01 and 05 of the Bol Marathi course.
The pattern is simple: name first, then the closing आहे. The verb-final order from English→Marathi greetings carries over -- just slot your details in.
tip: Pair माझं नाव ... आहे with तुम्ही कुठे राहता? (Where do you live?) -- the two sentences that start every Marathi conversation.

sections.heading: The two-sentence starter kit
paragraphs: 1) माझं नाव ... आहे (My name is ...)  2) मी ... ला/मध्ये राहतो (I live in ... -- use ला for cities, मध्ये for areas). With these two, you have covered the first minute of any Marathi introduction.

sections.heading: Asking back -- the polite return
paragraphs: तुमचं नाव काय? (What is your name?) and तुम्ही कुठे राहता? (Where do you live?) use the same words you just learned -- flip the pronoun and you have a full exchange.

mistakes.why: Introduction sentences use the possessive + noun + आहे pattern, not the pronoun + आहे.

mistakes.right: पुणेला (city), महाराष्ट्रात (state), गावात (village) -- ला for cities, मध्ये/त for others
mistakes.why: Marathi case markers shift by place type; the curriculum drills ला with cities in Unit 05.

mistakes.right: मी पुणेला राहतो आहे -- verb + आहे always
mistakes.why: Continuous and simple present both end in आहे in Marathi course sentences.

mcq.question: "I live in Pune" in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: मी (I) + पुणेला (to Pune) + राहतो (live) -- verb last.

mcq.question: How do you ask "What is your name?"
mcq.explanation: तुमचं नाव काय? -- formal/respectful; तुझं is intimate only.

translate.source: I am Rahul. I live in Mumbai.
translate.answer: माझं नाव राहुल आहे. मी मुंबईला राहतो.
translate.note: Unit 01 + Unit 05 -- two sentences, one exchange.

faq.question: How do you say "Where are you from?" in Marathi?
faq.answer: तुम्ही कुठून आलात? -- literally "From where have you come?" (Unit 05 speaking).

faq.question: Can I use नमस्ते in Marathi introductions?
faq.answer: Use नमस्कार -- it is the standard Marathi greeting. नमस्ते marks you as a Hindi speaker immediately.

title: English to Marathi: Daily Needs & Essentials
description: Ask for water, food, help, the bathroom, and say you are hungry or tired -- Unit 02 survival sentences mapped English to Marathi.
intro: Six survival sentences from Unit 02: asking for water, food, help, the bathroom, and expressing hunger or tiredness. Each maps the English need to the Marathi sentence with a speaking tip.
The grammar lever here is the dative pattern मला ... पाहिजे (to me ... is needed) -- it covers water, food, help, and almost every concrete need.
tip: मला पाणी पाहिजे, मला चहा पाहिजे, मला मदत पाहिजे -- swap the noun, the frame stays identical. Learn one, you have them all.

sections.heading: The मला ... पाहिजे frame
paragraphs: English "I need X" becomes Marathi मला X पाहिजे -- literally "to me, X is needed". The noun (पाणी, चहा, मदत, शौचालय) slots in; the frame never changes.

sections.heading: Body states use the same logic
paragraphs: Hunger and thirst are also needs: मला भूक लागली आहे (hunger has struck me), मला तहान लागली आहे (thirst has struck me). The verb लागणे (to strike/hit) replaces पाहिजे for body states.

mistakes.wrong: Saying मी पाणी हवे for "I want water"
mistakes.why: हवे is colloquial; पाहिजे is the course standard and works for every need.

mistakes.wrong: Using मला for "I am hungry" as मला भूक आहे
mistakes.why: Hunger is not a static possession -- it arrives (लागणे). The course teaches the dynamic form.

mcq.question: "I need help" in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: मला मदत पाहिजे -- dative + noun + पाहिजे.

mcq.question: Where is the bathroom?
mcq.explanation: शौचालय कुठे आहे? -- the full sentence with आहे; dropping it is colloquial.

faq.question: How do you ask for water in Marathi?
faq.answer: मला पाणी पाहिजे -- the universal need sentence. In a hurry, पाणी! also works but the full sentence is polite by default.

faq.question: Is there a single word for "please"?
faq.answer: कृपया works, but the मला ... पाहिजे frame is already polite -- कृपया is optional.

title: English to Marathi: Asking & Giving Directions
description: How to ask where something is, understand left/right/straight, and give simple directions -- Unit 08 speaking sentences mapped English to Marathi.
secondaryKeywords: how to ask directions in marathi
intro: Six direction sentences from Unit 08: asking where a place is, understanding left/right/straight, and saying you are lost. Each maps the English phrase to the Marathi with the vocabulary you need at a street corner.
Marathi direction words (डावा, उजवा, सरळ, थांबा) are short and used exactly where English puts left/right/straight/stop -- no new grammar, just vocabulary swap.
tip: डावा = left, उजवा = right, सरळ = straight, थांबा = stop. Say them while walking -- muscle memory beats flashcards.

sections.heading: The four navigation words
paragraphs: डावा (left), उजवा (right), सरळ (straight), थांबा (stop) -- every direction sentence in Unit 08 is built from these four plus the question word कुठे (where).

sections.heading: Asking where something is
paragraphs: कुठे आहे? (Where is it?) works for anything -- स्टेशन कुठे आहे?, शौचालय कुठे आहे?, होटेल कुठे आहे? The answer will use the same four words: सरळ जा, डावीकडे वळा, उजवीकडे आहे.

mistakes.right: डावा/उजवा -- no sound overlap, must learn fresh
mistakes.why: Hindi बायाँ/दायाँ and Marathi डावा/उजवा share zero phonetics. This is pure vocabulary learning.
थांब is the root; the spoken command is थांबा (stop!) or थांबा एक मिनिट (wait a minute).

mcq.question: Left in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: डावा = left; उजवा = right.

mcq.question: "Go straight" in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: सरळ जा (straight go) -- the standard direction command.

mcq.question: Where is the station?
mcq.explanation: स्टेशन कुठे आहे? -- question word + subject + आहे.

faq.question: How do you say "turn right" in Marathi?
faq.answer: उजवीकडे वळा -- right-side turn. The verb वळणे (to turn) takes the direction word + एकडे.

faq.question: What is the word for "stop"?
faq.answer: थांबा -- use it with an auto driver: थांबा एक मिनिट (wait a minute) or just थांबा! (stop!).

title: English to Marathi: Shopping & Bargaining at the Market
description: Ask the price, name a quantity, bargain politely, accept, pay, and ask for the bill -- six Unit 09 sentences mapped English to Marathi.
intro: Six complete market sentences from Unit 09: asking the price, naming a quantity, bargaining politely, accepting, paying online, and asking for the bill. Each maps the English to the Marathi with a speaking tip.
The frame is identical to Hindi: quantity first (एक किलो), then the verb (द्या). Bargaining is a single line: थोडं कमी करा, कृपया.
tip: थोडं कमी करा, कृपया -- say it with a smile. Vendors expect it; it is polite, not rude.

sections.heading: The quantity + verb frame
paragraphs: English "Give me one kilo" → Marathi एक किलो भाजी द्या -- quantity (एक किलो) + noun (भाजी) + verb (द्या). The noun changes, the frame stays.

sections.heading: Bargaining & payment
paragraphs: थोडं कमी करा, कृपया (reduce a little please) -- the standard polite bargain. मी ऑनलाइन देनार (I'll pay online) and बिल द्या, कृपया (give the bill please) close the transaction.

mistakes.why: Hindi कितना/कितनी/कितने collapses to Marathi किती -- one word for all.
Marathi drops the nasal: महँगा → महाग, सस्ता → स्वस्त.
नकद is formal; रोख is the everyday Marathi word.

mcq.question: How much is this?
mcq.explanation: हे किती आहे? -- the standard price question.

mcq.question: Reduce a little, please.
mcq.explanation: थोडं कमी करा, कृपया -- exact Unit 09 line.

mcq.question: Cash in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: रोख (rokh) -- everyday word; नकद is formal.

faq.question: How do you bargain in Marathi?
faq.answer: थोडं कमी करा, कृपया -- reduce a little, please. The polite कृपया makes it standard etiquette.

faq.question: What is the word for "expensive"?
faq.answer: महाग -- same root as महँगा, nasal dropped.

title: English to Marathi: Technology, Phone & Internet
description: Tech, phone and internet sentences -- calling, messaging, Wi-Fi, charging, apps -- from Unit 12 speaking mapped English to Marathi.
intro: Six technology and phone sentences from Unit 12: making a call, sending a message, asking for Wi-Fi, charging the phone, downloading an app, and saying the battery is low. Each maps the English to the Marathi with the vocabulary you need on a modern Marathi phone screen.
Most tech words are English loans written in Devanagari: मोबाईल, इंटरनेट, व्हाट्सअॅप, चार्ज, अॅप, बैटरी -- the sentences just add the Marathi verbs around them.
tip: मोबाईल, इंटरनेट, चार्ज, अॅप, बैटरी -- these are the same words, just Devanagari. Learn the verbs (फोन करा, मेसेज पाठवा, चार्ज करा) and you have the full tech kit.

sections.heading: Loanwords you already know
paragraphs: मोबाईल (mobile), इंटरनेट (internet), व्हाट्सअॅप (WhatsApp), चार्ज (charge), अॅप (app), बैटरी (battery), व्हायफाय (Wi-Fi) -- the nouns are English loans in Devanagari. The Marathi part is the verb: फोन करा, मेसेज पाठवा, चार्ज करा, डाउनलोड करा.

sections.heading: Phone actions
paragraphs: फोन करा (make a call), मेसेज पाठवा (send a message), चार्ज करा (charge), डाउनलोड करा (download), ओपन करा (open). The verb करा (do/make) attaches to every tech noun.

mistakes.why: Marathi writes the English loan as मोबाईल; the Hindi spelling मोबाइल uses the wrong vowel sign.

mistakes.wrong: Saying इंटरनेट काम करत आहे for "internet is working"
mistakes.why: चालू = on/working; बंद = off. चालू/बंद is the standard on/off pair.

mcq.question: "Call me" in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: मला फोन करा -- to me, call (dative + verb).

mcq.question: "My battery is low" in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: माझी बैटरी कमी आहे -- battery is feminine, so माझी/कमी.

fill.sentence: व्हायफाय _____ आहे का? (Is the Wi-Fi on?)

faq.question: How do you say "WhatsApp" in Marathi?
faq.answer: व्हाट्सअॅप -- same word, Devanagari script. The verb is मेसेज पाठवा (send a message).

faq.question: What is "download" in Marathi?
faq.answer: डाउनलोड करा -- loanword + करा.

title: English to Marathi: Nature, Landscapes & Outdoors
description: Nature and landscape words -- mountains, rivers, trees, flowers, weather -- from Unit 14 speaking mapped English to Marathi.
intro: Six nature and landscape sentences from Unit 14: describing mountains, rivers, trees, flowers, and the weather. Each maps the English to the Marathi with the vocabulary from the Nature category (47 words).
Many nature words are Sanskrit loans shared with Hindi: पर्यावरण, प्रदूषण, हिम, नदी, पर्वत -- the shifts are in the everyday words: पेड़→झाड, तालाब→तलाव, फूल→फूल (same), चोटी→शिखर.
tip: झाड = tree (not पेड़), तलाव = lake (not तालाब), शिखर = peak (not चोटी). The Sanskrit-root words (पर्यावरण, हिम) are free -- the everyday ones are the ones to drill.

sections.heading: Landscape sentence frames
paragraphs: The sentences follow simple patterns: subject + complement + आहे (The mountain is high → डोंगर उंच आहे). The vocabulary comes from the 47-word Nature category.

sections.heading: Sacred trees & festival flowers
paragraphs: वड (banyan), पिंपळ (peepal), तुळस (holy basil), मोगरा (jasmine), झेंडू (marigold) -- these appear in festivals and daily rituals. Knowing them marks you as culturally literate, not just linguistically.

mistakes.why: पेड़ is Hindi; झाड is the Marathi word -- no sound overlap.
तालाब is Hindi; तलाव is Marathi. The -व- → -व- shift is regular.
चोटी is Hindi; शिखर is Marathi. Both Sanskrit roots, different forms.

mcq.question: Tree in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: झाड (jhāḍ) -- the everyday word; वृक्ष is formal/Sanskrit.

mcq.question: River in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: नदी (nadī) -- identical to Hindi, free vocabulary.

mcq.question: Mountain/peak in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: शिखर (śikhar) = peak/summit; डोंगर = mountain/hill.

faq.question: What is the Marathi word for "tree"?
faq.answer: झाड (jhāḍ) -- the everyday word; वृक्ष is formal.

faq.question: Are nature words similar to Hindi?
faq.answer: Sanskrit loans (पर्यावरण, प्रदूषण, हिम, नदी, पर्वत) are identical. Everyday words shift: पेड़→झाड, तालाब→तलाव, चोटी→शिखर.

title: English to Marathi: Transport, Travel & Getting Around
description: Trains, buses, autos, tickets, platforms, stations -- Unit 15 travel sentences mapped English to Marathi.
intro: Six transport and travel sentences from Unit 15: asking which train, booking online, finding the platform, describing the journey, booking a hotel, and taking an auto to the station. Each maps the English to the Marathi with the 25-word transport vocabulary.
The vocabulary splits: rail (आगगाडी, रेल्वे, स्टेशन, प्लॅटफॉर्म, तिकीट), road (बस, ऑटो, रिक्षा, गाडी, दुचाकी), air (विमान, विमानतळ), directions (डावा, उजवा, सरळ, थांबा).
tip: आगगाडी = train (formal), ट्रेन = train (everyday), रेल्वे = railway system. All three are correct; आगगाडी is the native word.

sections.heading: The station triangle
paragraphs: स्टेशन (station) + प्लॅटफॉर्म (platform) + तिकीट (ticket) -- the three words that get you on the train. Add आगगाडी/ट्रेन and you have the full rail kit.

sections.heading: Street transport
paragraphs: ऑटो/रिक्षा (auto rickshaw), बस (bus), टॅक्सी (taxi), दुचाकी (two-wheeler), सायकल (bicycle) -- the words for the last-mile journey from station to destination.

mistakes.wrong: Using रेल्वे for the train vehicle
mistakes.right: रेल्वे = railway system; आगगाडी/ट्रेन = the train
mistakes.why: रेल्वे is the network; the moving vehicle is आगगाडी or ट्रेन.
Cross-category polyseme -- the travel word बोट (boat) and the body word बोट (finger) are identical. Context disambiguates.
Hindi बायाँ/दायाँ have no sound overlap -- these are fresh learning.

mcq.question: Which train goes to Mumbai?
mcq.explanation: मुंबईला जाणारा ट्रेन कोणता? -- exact Unit 15 sentence.

mcq.question: Platform five in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: प्लॅटफॉर्म नंबर पाच आहे -- the full sentence from Unit 15.

mcq.question: Auto rickshaw in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: ऑटो and रिक्षा are both used interchangeably.

fill.sentence: _____ घेऊन स्टेशनला गेले. (Took auto to station.)

faq.question: How do you say "train" in Marathi?
faq.answer: Two words: आगगाडी (native) and ट्रेन (loan) -- both standard. रेल्वे means the railway system, not the vehicle.

faq.question: What is the word for "auto rickshaw"?
faq.answer: ऑटो or रिक्षा -- both used interchangeably.

title: English to Marathi: Time, Clock & Seasons
description: Tell time, name day parts, and talk seasons -- clock words, half-hours, monsoon, winter -- Unit 16 sentences mapped English to Marathi.
intro: Six time and season sentences from Unit 16: telling the clock (आता साडे पाच वाजले), day parts (सकाळ, दुपार, संध्याकाळ, रात्र), the week/month/year, and monsoon rain. Each maps the English to the Marathi with the vocabulary from the Time category (15 words).

The grammar key: Marathi says the clock "has struck" -- वाजले is the verb. साडे पाच वाजले = half past five (literally "five-and-a-half have struck"). The half-hour marker साडे is the only new grammar piece.
tip: साडे पाच वाजले = half past five. साडे + number + वाजले gives you every half-hour. The full hour is just पाच वाजले.

sections.heading: The वाजले clock
paragraphs: English "it is five o'clock" → Marathi पाच वाजले (five struck). English "half past five" → साडे पाच वाजले (five-and-a-half struck). The verb वाजले (struck) does the work of both "is" and "o'clock".

sections.heading: Day parts and the काल trap
paragraphs: सकाळ (morning), दुपार (afternoon), संध्याकाळ (evening), रात्र (night) -- the four day parts. The big trap: काल = yesterday in Marathi (not tomorrow). Tomorrow is उद्या. This is the #1 calendar false friend for English/Hindi speakers.

mistakes.why: Marathi uses the verb वाजले (struck); बजे is Hindi.
Hindi कल does both; Marathi splits them. This is the single most dangerous false friend on the calendar.
गर्मी = heat (noun); उन्हाळा = the season. The word is different.

mcq.question: Half past five in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: साडे पाच वाजले -- साडे = half, वाजले = struck.

mcq.question: Tomorrow in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: उद्या = tomorrow. काल = yesterday -- the trap.

mcq.question: Monsoon season in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: पावसाळा (pāvasāḷā) -- the monsoon season.

fill.sentence: आता _____ वाजले. (It is now half past five.)

faq.question: How do you say "5 o'clock" in Marathi?
faq.answer: पाच वाजले -- the verb वाजले (struck) replaces Hindi बजे.

faq.question: What is the biggest time trap for English speakers?
faq.answer: काल means yesterday, not tomorrow. Tomorrow is उद्या. The verb वाजले (struck) replaces 'o'clock'.

title: English to Marathi: Hobbies, Free Time & Likes
description: Talk about what you like to do -- reading, cricket, music, painting -- the मला ... आवडतं pattern and adverbs of frequency from Unit 18.
intro: Six hobby and free-time sentences from Unit 18: saying what you like (मला वाचन आवडतं), how often (रोज, कधीकधी), and what you do in free time (cricket, music, painting). Each maps the English to the Marathi with the मला ... आवडतं frame.
The grammar key: likes happen TO you -- मला वाचन आवडतं = to-me reading is-pleasing. This mirrors Hindi मुझे पढ़ना पसंद है exactly. Adverbs (रोज, कधीकधी) sit right before the verb.
tip: मला [activity] आवडतं -- swap the activity noun (वाचन, संगीत, क्रिकेट, चित्रकला) and the frame never changes.

sections.heading: The मला ... आवडतं frame
paragraphs: English "I like reading" → Marathi मला वाचन आवडतं. The liking happens TO you (मला = to me). Any activity noun drops in: मला संगीत आवडतं, मला क्रिकेट आवडतं, मला चित्रकला आवडतं.

sections.heading: Frequency adverbs sit before the verb
paragraphs: रोज (daily), कधीकधी (sometimes), नेहमी (always), कधीच (never) -- these sit right before the verb: मी रोज क्रिकेट खेळतो, मी कधीकधी चित्रकला करतो. Unit 18 drills this position consistently.

mistakes.wrong: Saying मी आवडतो वाचन for "I like reading"
mistakes.why: The liking happens TO you -- मला (to me) + noun + आवडतं. मी (I) is the wrong case.

mistakes.right: Adverb before verb: मी रोज खेळतो (not मी खेळतो रोज)
mistakes.why: Unit 18 pattern -- adverbs pre-verb, consistently.

mcq.question: "I like music" in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: मला संगीत आवडतं -- the frame is fixed: मला + noun + आवडतं.

mcq.question: I play cricket daily in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: मी रोज क्रिकेट खेळतो -- adverb रोज before verb खेळतो.

mcq.question: Sometimes I paint in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: मी कधीकधी चित्रकला करतो -- Unit 18 sentence.

faq.question: Why does "I like" use मला instead of मी?
faq.answer: आवडणे works like Hindi मुझे ... पसंद है -- the liking happens TO you. So मला (to me) + thing + आवडतं.

faq.question: How do you say "I like cricket" in Marathi?
faq.answer: मला क्रिकेट आवडतं -- same frame, swap the noun.

title: English to Marathi: Workplace, Office & Career Talk
description: Office sentences -- job, salary, meeting, leave, project, promotion, interview -- Unit 19 speaking mapped English to Marathi.
intro: Six workplace and career sentences from Unit 19: studying engineering, having an interview, working in an office, finishing a project, getting a promotion, and business doing well. Each maps the English to the Marathi with the vocabulary from the Work category (42 words).
Traditional occupations double as surnames in Maharashtra -- सुतार, लोहार, सोनार, शिंपी, न्हावी, धोबी -- knowing the word means you recognize the surname too.
tip: नोकरी = job, पगार = salary, बैठक = meeting, सुट्टी = leave, प्रमोशन = promotion. The modern office words are English loans; the traditional ones are pure Marathi.

sections.heading: Modern office essentials
paragraphs: नोकरी (job), पगार (salary), बैठक (meeting), सुट्टी (leave), संगणक (computer), प्रोजेक्ट (project), प्रमोशन (promotion), इंटरव्यू (interview) -- the words for your first day, your payslip, your career growth.

sections.heading: Traditional professions = surnames
paragraphs: सुतार (carpenter), लोहार (blacksmith), सोनार (goldsmith), शिंपी (tailor), न्हावी (barber), धोबी (washerman), माळी (gardener), गवळी (milkman) -- identical words serve as job titles and family names across Maharashtra.

mistakes.why: Hindi सिपाही = soldier; Marathi शिपाई is the office attendant. The soldier is सैनिक -- direct false friend.
मला काम आहे (I have work to do) vs माझी नोकरी आहे (I have a job).

mistakes.right: मालक/अधिकारी -- बॉस is understood but मालक is the Marathi word
mistakes.why: Loanwords work but native terms carry more respect in formal contexts.

mcq.question: Salary in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: पगार (pagār) -- everyday word; वेतन is formal.

mcq.question: A tailor in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: शिंपी (śimpī) = tailor; the surname Shimpī comes from this.

mcq.question: "I got a promotion" in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: मला प्रमोशन मिळालं -- dative + noun + मिळालं (got).

fill.sentence: उद्या माझं _____ आहे, तयार राहा. (Tomorrow my interview is, be ready.)

faq.question: What is the Marathi word for "salary"?
faq.answer: पगार (pagār) -- everyday; वेतन is formal/official.

faq.question: Are traditional professions also surnames?
faq.answer: Yes -- सुतार, लोहार, सोनार, शिंपी, न्हावी, धोबी, माळी, गवळी are both job titles and common surnames in Maharashtra.
